items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: I have been involved with this BMI Composer’s Workshop with Manny Albam and Jim McNeeley.

ctx.x: I’ve often wondered about — I do some writing myself, and I wonder sometimes about, let’s suppose I had a decent amount of money to spend, and I was going to commission you to write something. Is it easier for you if you have no guidelines, or if you have some guidelines?

Very good question. I have to say right now I would prefer none. However, that means you have to accept whatever you get. Now generally someone says well this is the ensemble that I want. But they don’t tell you what to write. That’s okay. And I’ve learned to arrange, and that’s different too. But you know, someone gave me a choice, and I have © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

been involved with this BMI Composer’s Workshop with Manny Albam and Jim McNeeley. Brookmeyer started it but I got a chance to be around all of those guys. And so they’re really composers, I mean serious composers. But Manny was like a composer, but he was really like, we used to call him the “half hour of the incredible arrangers.” He could come up, in a half hour, he would have an arrangement that would just sound great. And that’s a skill, a true skill. But my very — yeah I guess it was my first real…
